subject: sociology
title: Health
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Health.

concepts.def: The dominant Western view that health is the absence of biological disease, treated by medical experts focusing on the body rather than social causes.
The view that health and illness are shaped by social factors such as poverty, environment and lifestyle, not by biology alone.
Talcott Parsons' idea that being ill is a temporary social role with rights (exemption from normal duties) and obligations (to seek help and try to recover).
The process by which everyday or social conditions, such as sadness or childbirth, come to be defined and treated as medical problems.
Systematic differences in health and life expectancy between social groups by class, gender or ethnicity, often linked to material conditions.
The idea that what counts as 'illness' varies between cultures and over time, so definitions of health are shaped by society rather than fixed.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Health — a core area of A-Level Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Health brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Health.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The biomedical model defines health as:
options: Social wellbeing
The absence of biological disease
Being wealthy
Simply feeling happy

mcqs.q: Parsons' 'sick role' suggests an ill person is:
options: Permanently excluded from society
Temporarily exempt from duties but expected to seek help
Always morally to blame
Never given any rights
Curing all diseases
Redefining social conditions as medical problems
Closing hospitals down
Ignoring illness entirely

mcqs.q: Health inequalities are differences in health linked mainly to:
options: The weather
Social factors such as class and poverty
Personal choice only
Pure chance

mcqs.q: Does the social model say biology is irrelevant to health?
options: No - it argues social factors also strongly shape health, alongside biology.
The social model ignores the body entirely.
It means everyone defines health in the same way.
It claims only the rich ever get ill.
It means everyone defines health in the same way.
Treating non-medical or everyday conditions as medical problems.
It means closing down hospitals.
It simply means curing more diseases.

mcqs.q: Why do sociologists say illness is socially constructed?
options: It means everyone defines health in the same way.
It means closing down hospitals.
Because what counts as illness varies across cultures and over time.
It means illnesses are not real.
